CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

motrack is an R package (v0.3.0) for generating and visualizing trajectories for Multiple Object Tracking (MOT) experiments. It produces object positions and trajectories as tibbles and exports them as delimited text. No compiled code.

Commands

Run from the repo root. Check which R is on the path (which Rscript); the location differs between machines.

# Install dependencies
Rscript -e 'devtools::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)'

# Load package for interactive work (no install needed)
Rscript -e 'devtools::load_all()'

# Run all tests
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'

# Run one test file (filter matches the name after "test-")
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "bounce-pair")'

# Regenerate NAMESPACE and man/ from roxygen comments (RoxygenNote 7.3.3)
Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'

# Full R CMD check (CI runs it on macOS, Windows, Ubuntu devel/release/oldrel)
Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'

# Build the pkgdown site (CI: .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml)
Rscript -e 'pkgdown::build_site()'
  • There is no flag for a single test_that() block. Use testthat::test_file() after load_all(), or temporarily comment out the others.
  • devtools::load_all() and test() abort if any Imports package is missing (circular, ggforce and animation are the usual ones). Install them. Do not work around this by editing DESCRIPTION.
  • Edit roxygen comments in R/*.R, then run devtools::document(). Do not hand-edit NAMESPACE or man/*.Rd. Running a roxygen2 version other than the one in RoxygenNote rewrites DESCRIPTION, so check git diff DESCRIPTION afterwards.
  • There is no lint configuration.

Architecture

The package is a single simulation pipeline. Each function lives in its own file named after it, so find code with R/<function_name>.R.

Data model. Everything is a tibble with an object column (object IDs): - Position: object, x, y plus optional direction (radians; 0 = 3 o’clock, counter-clockwise) and speed. Validated by is_valid_position() (requires all three columns, finite numeric x/y, at least one row, unique non-NA object). - Trajectory: time, object, x, y plus direction, speed, and step-specific state columns (ttt for zigzag; ttc, mov_state, speed_scale for wait-and-move). Validated by is_valid_trajectory(). - position8c and trajectory8c (in data/, built by data-raw/trajectory8c.R) are example datasets.

Settings. Settings are a plain named list. default_settings() defines the valid keys; new_settings() overrides them and rejects unknown names. It also accepts two optional keys, speed and arena_inside_radius, which are not in the defaults.

Speed. settings$speed (or a speed column in the start position) is either a number or a list of functions function(time, moment) (write c(f) to wrap a single function). cur_speed() evaluates it, and it is called only from extrapolate_moment(), so every step function that moves objects through extrapolate_moment() supports function speeds. step_vortex reads settings$speed as a plain number and does not. step_waitandmove scales movement through its speed_scale column instead of changing speed.

Generation pipeline. 1. generate_positions_random(n, settings) (or generate_positions_grid()) places objects in a square/circle/donut arena (xlim/ylim, arena_shape), optionally enforcing min_distance. 2. make_random_trajectory(start, timescale, settings, step_function, ...) iterates over timescale. Each step first applies the enabled bounce functions (bounce_off_square, bounce_off_circle, bounce_off_inside, bounce_off_others) to the current moment, then calls step_function(moment, time_next, settings, ...). The result is a list-column of per-time moments that is unnested at the end. 3. Step functions (step_direct, step_zigzag, step_waitandmove, step_vonmises) return the next moment. They carry per-object state in extra columns, initialized on the first call (the if (!"ttt" %in% names(moment)) pattern). Custom steps should follow the same signature and use extrapolate_moment() to move objects and cur_speed() for speed.

Bouncing works on direction vectors and the next-step positions. bounce_off_others uses single-linkage clustering (hclust/cutree) on next-step distances to find collisions. bounce_pair does the two-body case.

Post-processing and output. - simplify_trajectory() reduces the per-frame data to critical points (first, last and direction changes, using wrapped angle differences). With snapshot = TRUE it keeps all objects at every critical time. With FALSE it keeps only each object’s own critical rows, with the original columns untouched. - estimate_position_for_time() (internal) linearly interpolates x/y between the two neighbouring frames. It is used for rendering simplified trajectories. All other columns, including time, come from the earlier frame. - plot_position(), plot_trajectory(), annotate_image(), annotate_aperture() draw with ggplot2 and grid/png. - render_trajectory_video() uses the animation package and needs an external ffmpeg (path set via animation::ani.options). - save_trajectory() / load_trajectory() read and write delimited text (delim argument) as time, x1, y1, x2, y2, ... with no header. - validate_trajectory() and validate_object_direction_change() check output.

Tidy evaluation. Code uses dplyr verbs with .data$col pronouns. The package uses the native |> pipe internally.

Grid / vortex steps (experimental). step_vortex, step_grid and calculate_incomplete_vortex are documented but not exported (step_vortex and step_grid are absent from NAMESPACE; coords_to_vortex_coords is exported). step_vortex does not yet respect arena limits fully, step_grid resamples directions with an unbounded while (TRUE) loop, and they round positions to the grid. Check them before relying on them.

Internal helpers marked @noRd (no .Rd page): distances(), estimate_position_for_time(), calculate_incomplete_vortex().

Tests

Tests live in tests/testthat/ (one test-<name>.R per function or topic; testthat edition 3, based on the Config/testthat/edition in DESCRIPTION). Randomized tests call set.seed(). Internal functions can be called directly because tests run inside the package namespace.
